title: fix(scripts): route the last two fence-opening predicates through the shared authority
body:
Fixes #9331

Two sites decided whether a line OPENS a markdown fence, and neither was run-aware. Both now import `openFence` / `closesFence` from `scripts/markdown-fence-scan.mjs` (objectui#9194) and **both private spellings are deleted** — the value is in removing the copy, not in making a second copy correct.

## The two wrong answers

| site | private spelling | what it got wrong |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-prompt-component-keys.mjs:176` | `/^\s*(?:```\|~~~)/` used as a **toggle** | It flips on a run of ANY length, so a four-backtick opener was closed by the next three-backtick line — which CommonMark makes **body text**. From there the gate read code as prose and prose as code for the rest of the file. An ODD number of stray markers never resynchronises, so a real `**Keys:**` bullet after the wrapper went **invisible** and the gate reported OK over text it never looked at. |
| `check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs:341` | non-greedy ``/```(?:tsx?\|jsx?\|typescript)\n([\s\S]*?)```/g`` | Non-greedy ends the block at the FIRST three-backtick run after the opener, so an example written inside a longer wrapper ended at the quoted INNER marker and the gate parsed a **truncated** example. Half an example is still valid TSX — it parses clean, finds no hand-spelled reader in the half it never saw, and reports OK. |

Site 2's extraction loop is rewritten **line-based**, since a run-aware answer cannot be expressed as one regex. It is the larger half of the diff.

## The recurrence guard was itself half-blind

`markdown-fence-scan.test.ts` required an **anchored** regex literal (`/\^`), so it could only ever have caught the toggle — the shared reader's predicate was **unanchored** and would have walked straight past it. The anchor is now optional, all four gates are pinned, the positive control carries one line per spelling actually deleted, and a new **negative control** keeps the widened predicate off the legitimate inline-code regex (`` /`([^`]+)`/g ``) that `check-prompt-component-keys.mjs` really carries.

## Why the proof is not "the gate output changed"

Both defects are **latent**, so the output must NOT change. Measured on this base (`0a6372e3a9`), never asserted from memory:

- **Site 1 population** — 3 files, 627 lines under `.github/prompts/`. Lines the old predicate calls a marker: **34** (lit control, HIT). Runs of 4+ backticks: **0**. Lines where old and new disagree: **0**. Nonsense control: MISS.
- **Site 2 population** — 1439 source files, 16511 JSDoc blocks, 135 extracted fences. Old vs new extraction over every block: **16511 agree, 0 disagree**, both sides hashing to `0fe1e95ea83efe41f15931a2a0124f05bfa6180e93c34405936d5e6c0f99364c` over 30538 extracted chars (non-empty guard). The one 4-backtick construct on that surface is an inline code **span** on a prose line, not an opener — printed and read.
- **Gate stdout byte-identical** — `check:prompt-keys` `bc337bda…` (598 B) and `check:doc-example-readers` `d0d30a36…` (139 B), PRE == POST, both exit 0.

## Regression legs — they fail without the repair

Fixtures are arrays of string literals, never raw fences: a backtick run at the start of a line in these files would open a fence in the very gates the suites drive. Verified — **0** lines in either test file start with a backtick run (control: 7 such runs live inside string literals).

**Ablation.** With the fix in, each gate's local predicate was restored, the mutation proven on disk by `git hash-object` (`414740eb…` → `4530db8a…`, `fafd0aaf…` → `cbc89884…`), and **6 tests went RED**:

- `…shared-reader` › reads a four-backtick example whole, not truncated at the quoted marker
- `…shared-reader` › does not lift a tsx block quoted inside a markdown wrapper
- `…prompt-component-keys` › does not judge a bullet quoted inside the wrapper as a bullet
- `…prompt-component-keys` › still sees the real bullet after an ODD number of markers
- `markdown-fence-scan` › `check-prompt-component-keys.mjs` spells no fence predicate of its own
- `markdown-fence-scan` › `check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` spells no fence predicate of its own

Restore proven by hash equality to the HEAD blob plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, and by zero surviving `ABLATION_LOCAL_FENCE` markers — never by an editor's exit code. The four **lit controls** (ordinary three-backtick fence, an unfenced bullet, a non-code language, an unterminated fence) stayed green throughout, so the cases above cannot pass by masking or extracting nothing.

## Verification

| command | PRE | POST |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node scripts/check-prompt-component-keys.mjs` | 0 | 0 (byte-identical) |
| `node scripts/check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` | 0 | 0 (byte-identical) |
| `node scripts/markdown-fence-scan.mjs` (self-test) | 0 | 0 |
| `vitest run` × 3 suites | 84 passed | **95 passed** (11 new) |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 | 0 — `--listFiles` confirms all 3 edited suites are in the type program (not NOT-MEASURED) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | — | 0 ("no changeset is owed"; an empty-frontmatter one is included anyway) |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | — | 0 (7591 tracked files) |

Exit codes captured by redirect-then-capture, never across a pipe.

`Bundle Analysis` is red across this lane and is not a required context — not touched by this change.

## Follow-up commit: the docblock this PR falsified (PM review)

`markdown-fence-scan.mjs` justified not capping indentation by measuring that the 12 over-indented markers all sit in `.github/prompts/component.prompt.md`, **"which is on neither gate's scan surface"**. That was true when written, of the two gates the module then served — and the first commit here falsified it: `check-prompt-component-keys.mjs` became a consumer and its scan surface is exactly `.github/prompts` (its `PROMPT_DIR`).

Corrected in `944e4144dd`, **prose only**. The cap is still NOT applied and no predicate changed; what changed is that the deferred card now has a named blast radius instead of none — capping would change how that gate reads **six blocks** of `component.prompt.md`, from fenced code it skips to prose it judges. Nothing moves today, because this module and both predicates it replaced all accept any leading whitespace — which is exactly what makes the conversion behaviour-neutral on that file.

The count is restated as a **dated reading**, following the convention objectui#9426 landed in `tsconfig.tier-base.json` ("re-derive rather than trusting this block if it matters"). Re-derived on this branch, not recalled: 34 marker lines under `.github/prompts/**`, **22** indented 0–3 (control, HIT) and **12** indented 4 — all in `component.prompt.md` (lines 57, 68, 99, 107, 115, 123, 129, 139, 164, 171, 202, 208), pairing into **6** fenced blocks. Nonsense control (indent > 100): MISS.

**Proven, not asserted, that this is prose only:**

- Every changed line is a comment line (`git diff` filtered to non-comment changes: empty).
- The file's code **tokens** hash identically before and after — `a10d6374df6037be`, 2926 chars on both sides — with a negative control confirming a real code edit breaks that equality. (A positional `maskComments` hash reported "differ" here; that reader was wrong, not the code: masking preserves offsets, so a longer docblock shifts every later byte.)
- Both gates' stdout is **still byte-identical to the PRE baseline**: `check:prompt-keys` `bc337bda…` and `check:doc-example-readers` `d0d30a36…`, both exit 0 — so nothing reads this docblock as data.
- `markdown-fence-scan --self-test` 0 · 3 suites 95/95 · `type-check:scripts` 0 · `check-control-bytes` 0 (7592 files).
